group: Where is he in the process?

questions.text: Has he had his aged care assessment, and does he hold a Notice of Decision with a classification?
Has a Support at Home budget been allocated, or is he still on the national priority queue?
Is he currently receiving CHSP, Veterans' Home Care, or a transitioned Home Care Package (no-worse-off rules)?
Is there a hospital discharge or other event creating urgency?

group: What does he need, and how will that change?

questions.text: Which daily tasks does he need help with now — showering, dressing, medication, meals, cleaning, garden, transport?
Are there clinical needs (wounds, diabetes, continence, falls, cognition, pain) that need a nurse rather than a support worker?
Is decline expected over 12–24 months, and is residential care or palliative care a likely end-point?
Would short-term restorative care (e.g. physio after a fall) help before ongoing services are set?

group: How does the PTSD shape the care?

questions.text: What are his known triggers — strangers in the house, unannounced visits, certain behaviours, gender of workers, loud equipment?
How much does continuity of the same one or two workers matter to him?
Who treats his PTSD now (GP, psychiatrist, Open Arms, psychologist), and should the provider liaise with them?
Does he want veteran-specific social connection (RSL sub-branch, Legacy, peer groups) as part of social support?

group: Which DVA services does he already use or qualify for?

questions.text: Which DVA card does he hold — Gold, or White (specific conditions)?
Is he already receiving Veterans' Home Care, DVA community nursing, Coordinated Veterans' Care, or MRCA household services/attendant care?
Which services should DVA fund so the Support at Home budget is kept for the rest?
Is the “army pension” a DVA Service Pension (means-tested) or military superannuation (DFRDB/MSBS)?
Has DVA issued his Support at Home contribution letter yet? If not, has the income and assets assessment been lodged?
Would he top up privately for extra hours beyond the budget?
Is anyone else's income or assets involved (partner)?
Does he live alone, or with a partner or family carer who needs respite or support?
Is the home safe as it is — steps, bathroom, rails, ramps, security, emergency alarm?
Does he drive? How far are his GP, specialists, pharmacy and hospital (QEII, PA)?
Are there pets, smoking, firearms or other worker-safety matters a provider will ask about?
Is there an enduring power of attorney, and should a family member be his registered supporter?
Who should receive statements, incident notices and care-plan reviews?
How tech-capable are he and the family — app, portal, email, paper?
Rank: same workers · lowest price · clinical depth · flexibility of times · local organisation · veteran ethos.
Are there faith, cultural or values preferences for the provider?
What would make him end a provider relationship?
